Summary:
Mark the AArch64 ELF fcontext assembly as BTI-compatible when the build
requests branch target enforcement (`-mbranch-protection=bti` or
`standard`, which define `__ARM_FEATURE_BTI_DEFAULT`).

The linker only marks an AArch64 shared library as BTI-compatible if
every input object carries the GNU_PROPERTY_AARCH64_FEATURE_1_BTI
property. These three objects have none, so any library that links
Boost.Context loses BTI even when the rest of it is built with branch
protection.

Add a `bti c` landing pad (encoded as `hint #34`, a NOP on CPUs without
BTI) at the start of `hoost_make_fcontext`, `hoost_jump_fcontext` and
`hoost_ontop_fcontext`, and emit the BTI property note. Each function
is entered by a call. Context switches resume through `ret`, including
the `finish` trampoline, which is reached through the link register,
and BTI does not check `ret`. There are no `br` or `blr` instructions
in these files, so entry landing pads are sufficient.

Builds without branch protection are unchanged. Record the change in
`external/boost/README.md`.

Reviewed By: tmikov, oskarwirga

Differential Revision: D128389488
